deep_dive_html:
The Perils of Undefined Operating Expenses

For dental practitioners, a commercial lease is more than a real estate agreement; it is a foundational component of your practice's overhead. Common Area Maintenance (CAM) clauses are frequently the primary vehicle through which landlords erode tenant profitability. In many medical-retail leases, landlords attempt to pass through not just routine maintenance, but significant capital expenditures—such as parking lot resurfacing, structural repairs, or HVAC replacements—under the guise of 'operating expenses.'

The danger lies in the lack of specificity within the lease's definition of 'Operating Expenses.' An unscrutinized CAM clause may allow the landlord to include administrative fees, management markups, and even 'controllable' expenses that are subject to sudden, massive spikes. For a dental office, where predictable monthly overhead is critical for managing staff, specialized equipment depreciation, and patient acquisition costs, an uncapped CAM escalation can turn a profitable practice into a financial liability overnight.

Strategic Protections for Medical Tenants

To safeguard your practice, you must move beyond accepting the landlord's standard 'triple net' (NNN) language. A sophisticated lease negotiation focuses on three critical pillars of CAM protection:

  • Controllable Expense Caps: Negotiate a fixed percentage cap (typically 3-5%) on 'controllable' expenses, ensuring that costs like landscaping, cleaning, and security do not fluctuate wildly year-over-year.
  • Capital Expenditure Exclusions: Explicitly exclude any costs related to the replacement of structural elements or major systems—such as the roof, foundation, or primary plumbing—from the CAM pool, unless they are specifically amortized over their useful life and only the annual portion is passed through.
  • Audit Rights and Transparency: Ensure the lease grants you the right to audit the landlord's books and records to verify that the expenses being billed are legitimate, documented, and compliant with the lease terms.
